q-46125.name: Question 1
q-46125.problem: A car travels at $1\,000$ meters per minute. In kilometers, how far will the car travel in one hour?
q-46125.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.$ We're converting two units instead of just one, so we're going to have to multiply by two conversion factors:

$$
\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

One of the conversion factors should change $\text{m}$ to $\text{km}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{m}}}{\text{min}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{m}}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

The other conversion factor should change $\text{min}$ into $\text{hour}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{m}}}{\cancel{\text{min}}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{m}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{min}}}{\text{hour}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\text{m}}\cdot \frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The rate given in the problem statement is $1\,000\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}}.$

- There are $1\,000$ meters per kilometer, therefore, there are $\frac{1}{1\,000}$ kilometers per meter.

- There are $60$ minutes in one hour.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}1000\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}} & =1000\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}}\cdot \frac{1}{1\,000}\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{m}}\cdot 60\,\frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}} \\  & =1000\cdot \frac{1}{1\,000}\cdot 60(\frac{\cancel{\text{m}}}{\cancel{\text{min}}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{m}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{min}}}{\text{hour}}) \\  & =60\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, a speed of $1\,000$ meters per minute is equivalent to $60$ kilometers per hour. Thus, the car will travel $60$ kilometers in one hour.

q-46125.html:
Question 1
?

A car travels at 1000 meters per minute. In kilometers, how far will the car travel in one hour?

a
20km
b
100km
c
40km
d
80km
e
60km
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given the units mmin, and we want to convert this into kmhour. We're converting two units instead of just one, so we're going to have to multiply by two conversion factors: mmin⋅??⋅??=kmhour

One of the conversion factors should change m to km. mmin⋅kmm⋅??=kmhour

The other conversion factor should change min into hour. mmin⋅kmm⋅minhour=kmhour

So, our conversion formula is mmin⋅kmm⋅minhour=kmhour.

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The rate given in the problem statement is 1000mmin.
  • There are 1000 meters per kilometer, therefore, there are 11000 kilometers per meter.
  • There are 60 minutes in one hour.

Applying our conversion formula, we have 1000mmin=1000mmin⋅11000kmm⋅60minhour=1000⋅11000⋅60(mmin⋅kmm⋅minhour)=60kmhour.

Consequently, a speed of 1000 meters per minute is equivalent to 60 kilometers per hour. Thus, the car will travel 60 kilometers in one hour.

q-46132.name: Question 2
q-46132.problem: At the start of a launch, a space rocket consumes about $150$ kilograms of fuel per second. How much fuel does it consume per minute?
q-46132.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{s}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

$$
\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{s}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}
$$

We want to replace $\text{s}$ with $\text{min}.$ To get rid of $\text{s},$ we can put $\text{s}$ in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\text{min},$ we can put $\text{min}$ in the denominator.

$$
\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{s}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{s}}}{\text{min}}=\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{\text{s}}{\text{min}}=\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The rate given in the problem statement is $150\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{s}}.$

- There are $60$ seconds per minute.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}150\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{s}} & =150\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{s}}\cdot 60\,\frac{\text{s}}{\text{min}} \\  & =(150\cdot 60)\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{s}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{s}}}{\text{min}} \\  & =9\,000\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the space rocket consumes $9\,000$ kilograms per minute.

q-46132.html:
Question 2
?

At the start of a launch, a space rocket consumes about 150 kilograms of fuel per second. How much fuel does it consume per minute?

a
90000kg/min
b
9000kg/min
c
600kg/min
d
900kg/min
e
6000kg/min
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given the units kgs, and we want to convert this into kgmin. To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

kgs⋅??=kgmin

We want to replace s with min. To get rid of s, we can put s in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce min, we can put min in the denominator.

kgs⋅smin=kgmin

So, our conversion formula is

kgs⋅smin=kgmin.

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The rate given in the problem statement is 150kgs.
  • There are 60 seconds per minute.

Applying our conversion formula, we have 150kgs=150kgs⋅60smin=(150⋅60)kgs⋅smin=9000kgmin.

Thus, the space rocket consumes 9000 kilograms per minute.

q-46322.name: Question 3
q-46322.problem: The cheetah is considered the fastest land animal. It can achieve a speed of $120$ kilometers per hour. What is this speed in kilometers per minute?
q-46322.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}
$$

We want to replace $\text{h}$ with $\text{min}.$ To get rid of $\text{h},$ we can put $\text{h}$ in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\text{min},$ we can put $\text{min}$ in the denominator.

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{h}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{h}}}{\text{min}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}\cdot \frac{\text{h}}{\text{min}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The rate given in the problem statement is $120\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}.$

- There are $60$ minutes per hour. Taking the reciprocal, there are $\frac{1}{60}$ hours per minute.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}120\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}} & =120\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}\cdot \frac{1}{60}\,\frac{\text{h}}{\text{min}} \\  & =(120\cdot \frac{1}{60})\,\frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{h}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{h}}}{\text{min}} \\  & =2\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the cheetah can run at a speed $2\,\text{km}/\text{min}.$

q-46322.html:
Question 3
?

The cheetah is considered the fastest land animal. It can achieve a speed of 120 kilometers per hour. What is this speed in kilometers per minute?

a
2kmmin
b
20kmmin
c
0.5kmmin
d
0.2kmmin
e
5kmmin
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given the units kmh, and we want to convert this into kmmin. To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

kmh⋅??=kmmin

We want to replace h with min. To get rid of h, we can put h in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce min, we can put min in the denominator.

kmh⋅hmin=kmmin

So, our conversion formula is

kmh⋅hmin=kmmin.

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The rate given in the problem statement is 120kmh.
  • There are 60 minutes per hour. Taking the reciprocal, there are 160 hours per minute.

Applying our conversion formula, we have 120kmh=120kmh⋅160hmin=(120⋅160)kmh⋅hmin=2kmmin.

Thus, the cheetah can run at a speed 2km/min.
